addendum6.notes: THE V16 RECOVERY, and it works.  This is wave 23's V16X13 with the same 1,024-entry terminal diagonal re-solved at relative lambda 0.3 -- a rung that did not exist before this wave, because the fixed ladder jumps from 0.1 to 1.0 and wave 24 read the review moving non-monotonically inside exactly that gap.  Update scale 0.2165, held-out terminal logit SSE 0.2931 to 0.2091.  Identical parameters, 167,297,792, 0.728353x.  It reads SEVEN, and the ladder on this base is now unimodal with the peak at the new rung: no solve 5, lambda 1.0 6, lambda 0.3 SEVEN, lambda 0.1 6, lambda 0.01 5.  It carries THREE Useful lanes -- three distinct actions, the retrieval lane's three facts, and summarisation naming decision and the one-week slip and the weekly-schedule mitigation -- where the sealed source carried none.  It still loses the email, inverting the shipment dates as every child on this base does.  Three of sixteen lanes hit the cap.  The finding is not the seven; it is that a rung the solver's ladder does not contain is the best rung on the base, which means the atlas was never being walked, only sampled

axes.solve: absorbed by every downstream conditioned solve

axes.evidence: the sealed corpus, for a token OCCURRENCE census only; no activation, no capture, no forward pass
axes.heldout: not applicable: nothing is fitted.  What IS measured out of sample is the segmentation shift -- position agreement 1.0000 on the sealed corpus and 0.1460 on the frozen review prompts, with tokens-per-byte beside it
axes.selection: the 16384 rows kept by: every added/special token and every one of the 256 ByteLevel alphabet tokens (mandatory -- byte_fallback is false and there is no unk, so those 256 are the only reason an arbitrary byte can still be encoded), the transitive merge-tree closure of everything kept, and then the ranking (-census count, parent token id) until the budget is exactly met.  The census sums two streams over the sealed corpus: the donor-mapped ids the captures ran on and this tokenizer's own canonical segmentation of the same text.  With only 4633 observed tokens admitted beyond the mandatory set, the tie-break -- parent id order, which for a BPE table is its merge order and therefore its training-corpus frequency order -- decides most of this table, and that is stated rather than implied
axes.solve: NONE.  The rows are gathered verbatim; the identity gate is torch.equal against the source table's own bytes, not a tolerance.  The merge list is restricted to the closure (a merge survives iff its product and both operands are kept) and the ids are densely remapped, including the TemplateProcessing special-token ids, which carry hard ids a remap that missed them would silently corrupt

axes.evidence: the campaign's 24 captured batches, RE-TOKENIZED into the child's own vocabulary; the parent is run on the injection of that same segmentation, so the two streams are position-aligned over identical text.  No new corpus, no new prompt
axes.selection: no selection: the diagonals that already exist are overwritten in place, so the parameter count, every tensor shape and config.json are unchanged
axes.solve: prior-anchored ridge on the diagonal, closed form.  min_d ||Z diag(d) E^T - N diag(g) E^T||_F^2 + lambda ||d - g||^2 with Z the CHILD's RMS-normalised terminal residual on its OWN segmentation, N the PARENT's on the position-aligned injection of that same segmentation, E the child's tied table and g the parent's gain (also the prior).  Normal equations [(E^T E) o (Z^T Z)] d = [(E^T E) o (Z^T N)] g, one 1024x1024 SPD solve, no K-column target ever formed.  lambda on the internal fit split (wave-18 law), THE LAW a veto on update scale.  Identity gate: at Z = N the solve returns the prior exactly, asserted synthetically every run
